text:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: abnormal cross-region routing errors detected. Origin: eu-north-1 -> many requests routed to us-west-2 showing 502/504s and increased latency. 30m rolling error rate 18%. auto-signal: routing-policy-evaluator v2.3 returned inconsistent affinity. paging oncall.

alex-sre: ack — I'm on it, grabbing traces and checking routing tables. tagging @jon-netops for geo-dns checks.

jon-netops: seeing a pattern — a recent policy push (deploy id: rp-2026-03-15-42) changed region preference weights. Some probes show TTL still resolving to old pins but steer decisions flipped. curious: any canary notes? @liz-eng did you push anything?

liz-eng: I rolled the policy to test traffic at 09:12 UTC (small canary). health checks passed initially. I didn't expect fallback to start matching us-west for eu-north. rolling back canary now.

alex-sre: customer impact: maria-support reports multiple EU customers complaining about slow or 502s for embeddings endpoints. Ticket count up ~70. Tagging support for comms: @maria-support.

maria-support: confirmed — error spike aligns with the policy push window. CS is drafting a status blurb. no PII affected, mostly degraded responses and timeouts.

jon-netops: digging into DNS view: some resolver clusters still return geo records pointing to eu-north, others return us-west. suspect split brain in routing-policy-service; pushing a conservative revert to previous rule set.

alex-sre: plan: 1) revert rp-2026-03-15-42 to stable rp-2026-03-10-08 2) force low TTL drain for affected records to speed re-resolution 3) open temporary traffic-surge cap to reduce concurrent inflight. any objections?

liz-eng: no objections. initiating revert now.

incident-bot: action log: revert request submitted by liz-eng at 5554443338. Job id: revert-5554443338

jon-netops: issuing DNS TTL update:
```
# set TTL to 30s for geo records
curl -X POST https://internal-dns/api/v1/records/geo -d '{"ttl":30}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
```

alex-sre: also toggling fallback routing to prefer local region on mismatch. Command:
```
routingctl promote-fallback --region eu-north-1 --policy previous
```

incident-bot: routing policy revert completed (job revert-5554443338) — commit abcdef123 -> rp-2026-03-10-08

jon-netops: DNS TTL change propagated to most resolvers within 60s; some caches still 5m+ due to upstream. Monitoring re-resolves.

maria-support: CS update ready: "We are investigating increased errors for EU customers. A rollback of routing changes is in progress; expected improvement within 5-10 minutes. We'll follow up with a full post-incident update." :loudspeaker:

liz-eng: seeing immediate drop in 502s on eu-north probe fleet. latency normalizing. keeping canary disabled. leaving revert gated until telemetry stable for 10m.

alex-sre: oncall handoff: @oncall-rota i'll stay for handoff in 10m then hand to daytime SRE. current status: degraded -> recovering. outages impacted small subset of EU traffic, no data loss.

jon-netops: follow-ups: open a ticket to audit routing-policy-evaluator v2.3 for inconsistency during partial rollouts. also add stricter preflight check for geo affinity mismatch.

maria-support: CS will notify affected customers and attach ETA. no escalations yet.

incident-bot: severity downgraded to SEV3 at 5554443354 — metrics have returned to baseline and revert holding for observation. Incident channel will remain open for postmortem notes.

alex-sre: thanks all. postmortem action items: 1) rollback playbook rehearse 2) telemetry alert thresholds tuning 3) fix evaluator race during canary. I'll create the postmortem and assign owners.
